### G-KERNEL

| Id | Statement | Enforced by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| <span class="sl-id">G-KERNEL-01</span> | sandloom.core is layered (tooling > composition > contracts&RPC > auth&HTTP > drivers > messaging > persistence > bus > infra > foundation > config); every runtime import (module-level and function-local, only TYPE_CHECKING excluded) goes to the same or a lower layer, and the contract is exhaustive so a new sandloom.core child fails until placed. | `tests/architecture/test_kernel_import_contracts.py::test_kernel_import_contracts_are_kept`<br>import contract `kernel-layers` |
| <span class="sl-id">G-KERNEL-02</span> | The kernel has no import cycle at any depth (packages and modules, siblings of one layer included, sub-packages like unit_of_work.* / facade.*), counting function-local imports. | `tests/architecture/test_kernel_import_contracts.py::test_kernel_import_contracts_are_kept`<br>import contract `kernel-acyclic` |
| <span class="sl-id">G-KERNEL-03</span> | Configuration (sandloom.core.config: settings, tiers, accepted risks) is a leaf: it imports no other kernel package. | `tests/architecture/test_kernel_import_contracts.py::test_kernel_import_contracts_are_kept`<br>import contract `kernel-config-leaf` |
| <span class="sl-id">G-KERNEL-04</span> | No import contract has ignore_imports; should one ever appear it must carry a written '; reason:' line (refused otherwise) and import-linter fails an unmatched entry. | `tests/architecture/test_kernel_import_contracts.py::test_every_ignored_import_has_a_written_reason`<br>`tests/architecture/test_ledger_static_pins.py::test_import_contracts_have_no_ignore_imports`<br>import contract `kernel-layers`<br>import contract `kernel-acyclic`<br>import contract `kernel-config-leaf` |
| <span class="sl-id">G-KERNEL-05</span> | Every kernel function-local import (# noqa: PLC0415) states its category '- optional: <reason>' or '- cold: <reason>'; a cycle break is not a category and no kernel file is exempt. | `tests/architecture/test_lint_suppression_ratchet.py::test_kernel_function_local_imports_state_their_category` |
| <span class="sl-id">G-KERNEL-06</span> | Lint-suppression counts (noqa per rule) only go down, config-level ignores of ratcheted rules are pinned, and blind-except / bandit suppressions carry a reason. | `tests/architecture/test_lint_suppression_ratchet.py::test_noqa_counts_only_go_down`<br>`tests/architecture/test_lint_suppression_ratchet.py::test_config_level_ignores_of_ratcheted_rules_are_pinned`<br>`tests/architecture/test_lint_suppression_ratchet.py::test_blind_except_and_bandit_suppressions_carry_a_reason`<br>`tests/architecture/test_lint_suppression_ratchet.py::test_marker_scanner_reads_comments_only` |

### G-SAGA

| Id | Statement | Enforced by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| <span class="sl-id">G-SAGA-01</span> | register_saga refuses a malformed definition deterministically at registration (duplicate steps, missing compensation, steps on the wrong side of the pivot, more than one pivot, a call that is not a command) with a fix hint. | `sandloom/core/tests/test_sagas_definition.py::test_structure_is_refused_with_a_fix`<br>`sandloom/core/tests/test_sagas_definition.py::test_contract_problems_are_refused`<br>`sandloom/core/tests/test_sagas_definition.py::test_parameter_typo_names_the_fix`<br>`sandloom/core/tests/test_sagas_definition.py::test_a_remote_provider_is_checked_against_its_snapshot` |
| <span class="sl-id">G-SAGA-02</span> | Registering a saga adds a ContractRequirement for every called method to the module's consumes, so a missing provider fails startup. | `sandloom/core/tests/test_sagas_definition.py::test_requirements_cover_every_called_method`<br>`sandloom/core/tests/test_sagas_definition.py::test_register_saga_buffers_and_the_loader_merges_consumes` |
| <span class="sl-id">G-SAGA-03</span> | Saga instance tables are reached across tenants only through the audited system channel under tenant RLS. On every database, with or without tenant RLS, the runtime itself scopes saga state to the bound tenant (round 3) - saga_status and start_saga's create-or-get read only the bound tenant's instance (no tenant bound - only a tenant-less saga), so another tenant asking for a business id gets nothing (no instance id, status or step) and its start conflicts, and a nudge moves an instance only of the tenant it names; only the system channel (sweep, operator commands) and the test harness read across tenants (saga_store.ANY_TENANT, a required argument of every instance read). The bound tenant is read once the unit is open (round 4) - saga_status outside a unit opens its own, which binds SINGLE_TENANT_ID under TENANCY_MODE=single, so a canonical-tenant saga is found, not reported absent. | `sandloom/core/tests/test_sagas_channel.py::test_rls_databases_go_through_the_system_channel`<br>`sandloom/core/tests/test_sagas_channel.py::test_problem_only_for_rls_without_a_system_channel`<br>`sandloom/core/tests/test_sagas_ops.py::test_saga_state_never_crosses_tenants_without_rls`<br>`sandloom/core/tests/test_sagas_ops.py::test_single_tenant_status_and_start_see_the_canonical_tenants_saga` |
| <span class="sl-id">G-SAGA-04</span> | Every command step carries the derived operation key saga:<type>:<id>:<step>:do\|undo; non-deterministic arguments hit the command log's conflict and park the instance. | `sandloom/core/tests/test_sagas_definition.py::test_operation_key_rule`<br>`sandloom/core/tests/test_sagas_protocol.py::test_happy_path_runs_every_step_once_with_derived_keys`<br>`sandloom/core/tests/test_sagas_recovery.py::test_nondeterministic_args_hit_the_command_log_conflict_and_park` |
| <span class="sl-id">G-SAGA-05</span> | start_saga runs in the caller's Unit of Work (instance row and first nudge commit with the business change), is create-or-get on saga_id, conflicts on different input, and is refused outside a UoW. | `sandloom/core/tests/test_sagas_protocol.py::test_start_publishes_the_first_nudge_in_the_callers_transaction`<br>`sandloom/core/tests/test_sagas_ops.py::test_start_is_create_or_get_and_conflicts_on_other_input`<br>`sandloom/core/tests/test_sagas_ops.py::test_start_outside_a_unit_of_work_is_refused` |

| <span class="sl-id">G-DECL-06</span> | A typed event field with a wire name (Field(alias=...)) round-trips: publish() emits the alias, the registered and exported schema names it, and every reader (an @on consumer of the producer class or of a view, a projection, published(), deliver()) decodes it back from the wire key; @on and a projection bind the tenant from the field's wire name. | `tests/sdk/test_sdk_events.py::test_an_aliased_field_survives_publish_deliver_and_handler`<br>`tests/sdk/test_sdk_events.py::test_on_binds_the_tenant_by_its_wire_name`<br>`tests/sdk/test_sdk_testing_kit.py::test_an_aliased_field_survives_the_real_consumer_runtime` |
| <span class="sl-id">G-DECL-07</span> | SANDLOOM-C012. A contract DTO (a model / Enum a @contract signature names, nested ones included, except classes of sandloom.shared and generated copies) is held to the closed set of event wire shapes (G-DECL-01) within the contract wire types, plus what its generated copy can carry: no parametrised generic, a default the copy can write (JSON scalars, Enum members, UUID / Decimal / date / datetime / time / timedelta, containers of them) and default_factory only list / dict / set / frozenset / tuple, Field constraints only (no custom annotated constraint, no StringConstraints transformation, no callable discriminator, no exclude_if), no Flag enum; anything else is refused when @contract decorates the provider (ContractDtoError) naming the method, the field path and the fix. The copy carries fields, types and constraints, defaults, aliases (an alias_generator resolved per field), Literal / Enum values, nested and discriminated models and the allowed model_config options - never methods or validators, which stay the provider's; over the whole set (a property test over random payloads) the copy accepts and refuses exactly what the provider's class does, in python and JSON mode, and reads accepted payloads to the same data. Contract wire dumps use each field's wire name (by_alias), so an aliased DTO round-trips. | `tests/sdk/test_sdk_contract_dtos.py::test_a_dto_the_copy_cannot_carry_is_refused_with_its_path`<br>`tests/sdk/test_sdk_contract_dtos.py::test_the_copy_accepts_exactly_what_the_provider_accepts`<br>`tests/sdk/test_sdk_contract_dtos.py::test_every_copied_class_is_marked_and_carries_the_wire_shape`<br>`tests/sdk/test_sdk_contract_dtos.py::test_a_validator_stays_the_providers`<br>`tests/sdk/test_sdk_contract_dtos.py::test_a_caller_receives_the_copy_equal_to_the_providers_value` |

### C-PROJ

| Id | Statement | Enforced by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| <span class="sl-id">C-PROJ-01</span> | monotonic_upsert / monotonic_update apply a projection change only when the stored version is NULL or older than the incoming one, so at-least-once / out-of-order delivery never rolls a row back (tombstones block resurrection, and a tombstone purge never deletes one between an apply's watermark check and its write, as the apply holds the watermark row FOR SHARE until it commits). | `sandloom/core/tests/test_projection_upsert_guards.py::test_null_stored_version_is_updatable`<br>`sandloom/core/tests/test_projection_upsert_guards.py::test_tombstone_prevents_old_rebuild_from_resurrecting_deleted_entity`<br>`sandloom/core/tests/test_projections.py::test_consumer_applies_and_is_monotonic_and_idempotent`<br>`tests/sdk/test_sdk_projection_purge_race.py::test_a_purge_racing_an_apply_never_resurrects_a_relational_row` |
| <span class="sl-id">C-PROJ-02</span> | Projection rows carry tenant_id: monotonic_upsert requires it and raises TenantMismatchError if it differs from the bound tenant; updates are scoped to the bound tenant. | `sandloom/core/tests/test_projection_upsert_guards.py::test_upsert_requires_tenant_and_never_crosses_tenants`<br>`sandloom/core/tests/test_projection_upsert_guards.py::test_update_is_scoped_to_bound_tenant` |

| <span class="sl-id">C-MSTORE-01</span> | Delivery lattice laws (sandloom.core.guarantee_lattice): a guarantee's delivery set is closed under atomic => no_loss and no_dup; the meet is idempotent, commutative and associative, FULL is its unit on deliveries, and unknown properties are refused. | `sandloom/core/tests/test_guarantee_lattice.py::test_atomic_implies_no_loss_and_no_dup`<br>`sandloom/core/tests/test_guarantee_lattice.py::test_the_meet_is_a_semilattice_and_never_strengthens`<br>`sandloom/core/tests/test_guarantee_lattice.py::test_unknown_properties_are_refused` |
| <span class="sl-id">C-MSTORE-02</span> | Monotonicity: combining effects (the meet) never raises a guarantee above either operand. | `sandloom/core/tests/test_guarantee_lattice.py::test_the_meet_is_a_semilattice_and_never_strengthens` |
| <span class="sl-id">C-MSTORE-03</span> | Labels are derived from the mechanism, one scenario per row of the label table: only a write-store write is atomic; an outbox event is at-least-once (no_loss only with a durable bus); a durable consumer effect is no_dup only with the inbox in its database and the inbox outliving the stream; an effect in another store is no_dup only through a conditional write; a command is no_dup only with a database command log whose TTL covers the retries (never the cache fallback); consumer delivery is always qualified (parks_*); a label is shown only where it deviates. | `sandloom/core/tests/test_guarantee_lattice.py::test_each_row_of_the_label_table`<br>`sandloom/core/tests/test_guarantee_lattice.py::test_a_label_is_shown_only_when_it_deviates` |
| <span class="sl-id">C-MSTORE-04</span> | A conditional_write store passes conditional_write_conformance (older and duplicate versions never apply, tombstones are versioned and never resurrected, tenants isolated); the in-memory driver passes, a last-write-wins store fails. | `sandloom/core/tests/test_projection_kernel.py::test_the_memory_document_store_passes_the_conformance_kit`<br>`sandloom/core/tests/test_projection_kernel.py::test_the_conformance_kit_catches_a_store_without_the_version_guard`<br>`sandloom/core/tests/test_projection_kernel.py::test_the_memory_driver_advertises_and_passes_the_kit` |

| <span class="sl-id">C-DEPLOY-07</span> | An sandloom new application splits into microservices with no code change. sandloom add deploy <module>... --service <name> creates the app's microservices profile, nginx gateway and database init script from templates shipped in the package, then derives each service (its own database and migrate one-shot, RPC keys, worker and one beat), SERVICE_BINDINGS (plus the issuer's remote claims), RPC_ALLOWED_CALLS and the gateway routes from what the modules provide and consume. A repeated run changes nothing, a module is added to a service incrementally, hand edits outside the generated blocks are kept and an edit inside one is refused with a diff. The framework's own profile is the same generator's output. Route collection covers every route a service's app serves (round 3) - root-level routes (/ and /{slug} of module_router(prefix="")) get location = / and the catch-all location / (the internal surfaces then answering 404 explicitly), two services claiming the same route prefix, / or root-level parameter paths are refused with SANDLOOM-T014 naming them, never silently dropped, and a static catch-all left outside the generated routes block is refused. Each route prefix's locations stop at its segment boundary as Starlette matches (round 4) - location = /shop (to the service whose routes match the bare prefix) and location /shop/, never an unbounded location /shop, so /shopping stays with a root-level /{slug} service. | `sandloom/core/tests/test_scaffold_deploy.py::test_first_deploy_creates_the_profile_gateway_and_init_script`<br>`sandloom/core/tests/test_scaffold_deploy.py::test_a_split_app_passes_the_framework_split_invariants`<br>`sandloom/core/tests/test_scaffold_deploy.py::test_rerunning_is_idempotent`<br>`sandloom/core/tests/test_scaffold_deploy.py::test_adding_a_module_is_incremental_and_keeps_hand_edits`<br>`sandloom/core/tests/test_scaffold_deploy.py::test_a_hand_edit_inside_a_generated_block_is_refused_with_a_diff`<br>`sandloom/core/tests/test_scaffold_deploy.py::test_the_framework_profile_is_the_generators_output`<br>`sandloom/core/tests/test_scaffold_deploy.py::test_dev_env_covers_every_required_variable`<br>`sandloom/core/tests/test_scaffold_deploy.py::test_a_root_level_module_gets_the_root_and_the_catch_all`<br>`sandloom/core/tests/test_scaffold_deploy.py::test_two_services_claiming_root_level_paths_conflict`<br>`sandloom/core/tests/test_scaffold_deploy.py::test_a_hand_written_catch_all_outside_the_block_is_refused`<br>`sandloom/core/tests/test_scaffold_deploy.py::test_a_route_prefix_matches_only_its_own_segment`<br>`tests/e2e/test_app_split.py::test_an_sandloom_new_app_splits_into_microservices` |
| <span class="sl-id">C-DEPLOY-08</span> | A microservices profile is checked against the split invariants the framework's own profile is pinned to (SANDLOOM-T014), in sandloom test's schema & deploy step for an application's profile too, and every HTTP service boots alone with exactly its environment (settings, startup preflight, composition root, every consumed contract bound) without network. The gateway check compares the gateway with every route each service's app serves (root-level / and /{slug} included), never a prefix-filtered list (round 3), and samples adversarial paths (round 4) - each path parameter also takes every literal segment a route has at that position, bare and suffixed - requiring the upstream to be the service whose app routes match the path (Starlette matching, the most literal route winning). | `sandloom/core/tests/test_deploy_profiles.py::test_the_profile_passes_the_split_invariants_apps_are_checked_with`<br>`sandloom/core/tests/test_deploy_profiles.py::test_the_split_invariants_report_what_breaks_them`<br>`sandloom/core/tests/test_deploy_profiles.py::test_sandloom_test_checks_the_split_profile_of_a_project`<br>`sandloom/core/tests/test_deploy_profiles.py::test_every_service_boots_alone_with_its_bindings`<br>`sandloom/core/tests/test_scaffold_deploy.py::test_the_checker_finds_a_root_route_the_gateway_drops`<br>`sandloom/core/tests/test_scaffold_deploy.py::test_the_checker_samples_paths_that_collide_with_another_prefix` |

| <span class="sl-id">C-SDK-05</span> | The sandloom docs recipes with whole files (test-service-or-task, call-contract, projection-from-platform-events, event-v2, periodic-task) run as written in a generated app: their sandloom add / migrate new lines and # file: blocks in text order, then sandloom generate and sandloom test on the whole app and sandloom docs from the installed packages (tools/smoke/recipes_check.py, CI job app-recipes). | `tests/sdk/test_sdk_recipes.py::test_the_recipes_check_runs_every_verified_recipe`<br>`tests/sdk/test_sdk_recipes.py::test_recipe_parts_keep_the_text_order`<br>`tests/e2e/test_app_recipes.py::test_every_recipe_runs_in_a_generated_app` |
| <span class="sl-id">C-SDK-06</span> | sandloom.sdk ships the id and timestamp idiom: new_id() returns an RFC 9562 UUIDv7 (version 7, RFC 4122 variant, the current Unix millisecond) that strictly increases within a process (a burst in one millisecond, a clock stepping back, a full counter) and orders by time across processes; CreatedAt / UpdatedAt map timestamptz NOT NULL columns defaulting to clock_timestamp() (UpdatedAt also on update), compose with TenantScoped, autogenerate as server_default=sa.text('clock_timestamp()'), and rows one transaction inserts list in creation order by created_at then id. sandloom docs describes them and the list-order recipe; the bundled modules' chains migrate every such column to the clock_timestamp() default. | `tests/sdk/test_sdk_columns.py::test_new_id_is_a_uuid7_stamped_with_the_current_millisecond`<br>`tests/sdk/test_sdk_columns.py::test_ids_of_a_burst_strictly_increase`<br>`tests/sdk/test_sdk_columns.py::test_the_fallback_orders_one_millisecond_and_a_clock_step_back`<br>`tests/sdk/test_sdk_columns.py::test_the_fallback_moves_to_the_next_millisecond_when_the_counter_is_full`<br>`tests/sdk/test_sdk_columns.py::test_ids_of_different_processes_order_by_time`<br>`tests/sdk/test_sdk_columns.py::test_the_timestamp_columns_default_to_clock_timestamp`<br>`tests/sdk/test_sdk_columns.py::test_the_columns_compose_with_tenant_scoped`<br>`tests/sdk/test_sdk_columns.py::test_alembic_autogenerate_renders_clock_timestamp`<br>`tests/sdk/test_sdk_columns.py::test_rows_of_one_transaction_list_in_creation_order`<br>`tests/sdk/test_sdk_columns.py::test_sandloom_docs_describes_the_idiom`<br>`tests/integration/test_migrations_per_chain.py::test_chains_reproduce_orm_schema_exactly` |
| <span class="sl-id">C-SDK-03</span> | sandloom.sdk.tasks.shared_task is Celery's decorator typed with the task's signature (call, delay, apply_async, s), so a task module type-checks under strict mypy with no project override; cron() builds a beat schedule from a five-field expression. | `tests/sdk/test_sdk_generators.py::test_a_fully_generated_app_passes_the_static_gates` |

| <span class="sl-id">C-GEN-04</span> | sandloom add consumer writes a view from the producer schema (the tree or the exported file); without one it needs --field and marks the view unverified. | `tests/sdk/test_sdk_generators.py::test_add_consumer_takes_the_producer_schema_or_marks_unverified` |
| <span class="sl-id">C-GEN-05</span> | sandloom add saga writes package files only; an existing target is kept and the output written as *.new. | `tests/sdk/test_sdk_generators.py::test_an_existing_target_is_never_overwritten` |

| <span class="sl-id">C-GEN-08</span> | sandloom add module wires the module where its project loads modules (the framework tree's LOCAL_MODULES, SANDLOOM_MODULES lists, the monolith profile; an sandloom new app discovers it) and, in the framework tree, gives its tests the kit's fixtures (client, published recording) through a one-line conftest. | `tests/sdk/test_sdk_generators.py::test_add_module_in_the_framework_tree_is_wired_and_gets_the_kit` |

| <span class="sl-id">C-GEN-11</span> | sandloom add module generates a list route (GET /items) whose limit is capped with Query(le=...) over its TenantScoped table, newest first in a deterministic order (the model uses the framework's idiom - id defaults to new_id, a UUIDv7, and created_at is Mapped\[CreatedAt\], which defaults to clock_timestamp(), so rows created in one transaction do not tie - and the list orders by created_at then id), and a test that covers the order of rows created in one transaction, the page size, the cap (422) and another tenant's empty list. | `tests/sdk/test_sdk_generators.py::test_add_module_lists_items_capped_and_tenant_scoped`<br>`tests/sdk/test_sdk_generators.py::test_add_module_lists_newest_first_deterministically_in_one_transaction`<br>`tests/sdk/test_sdk_generators.py::test_a_fully_generated_app_passes_its_tests_up_to_the_h1_stubs`<br>`tests/sdk/test_sdk_columns.py::test_rows_of_one_transaction_list_in_creation_order` |

| <span class="sl-id">C-GEN-14</span> | Example apps pass their own gate - every example app (examples/*) and the tutorial app (docs/tutorial-app/*) passes the gate an app developer runs, sandloom test --ci --full (generated files checked, schema & deploy, the full suite, ruff check without fixing, ruff format, mypy, sandloom check, contract and route snapshots, migration drift), in the CI examples job, which lists every such app; a generated contract stub is exactly what ruff format writes. | `tests/architecture/test_ci_local_runner.py::test_every_example_and_the_tutorial_app_run_their_own_gate_in_ci`<br>`sandloom/core/tests/test_run_tests_cli.py::test_ci_never_writes_so_ruff_check_never_fixes`<br>`tests/sdk/test_sdk_generated.py::test_a_rendered_stub_is_what_ruff_format_writes`<br>`tests/sdk/test_sdk_generated.py::test_a_generated_stub_is_ruff_formatted` |
| <span class="sl-id">C-GEN-15</span> | sandloom generate \[module ...\] writes every generated file - module, route and contract snapshots, contract stubs, generated DTO copies, exported event schemas - after the compatibility checks (an incompatible change fails with its code and nothing is written; a weaker route policy is refused, pointing to sandloom routes snapshot --write); module names narrow it to those modules' files. sandloom test never writes a generated file, dev and --ci alike: a stale or hand-edited one fails, listed under "generated files are stale: run `sandloom generate`". ## Gaps

| Id | Size | Missing |
| --- | --- | --- |
| <span class="sl-id">C-EVENT-01</span> | S | No test proves that publish_event_versions inside a UoW writes all versions as outbox rows atomically (rolled back together). |
| <span class="sl-id">C-INFRA-05</span> | S | no test resolves a Capability(...) dependency in a request and asserts it yields the named provider (or the contract/feature error) |
| <span class="sl-id">C-INFRA-10</span> | S | no test calls the /diagnostics/infra endpoint itself (only registry.describe(); the route appears only in the operation-class map) |
| <span class="sl-id">C-MIGRATE-03</span> | S | Only flag plumbing is tested; no test runs upgrade-core --database <named> against a second database. |
| <span class="sl-id">C-OBS-06</span> | S | No test asserts Sentry init is a no-op without SENTRY_DSN / initialises with it. |
| <span class="sl-id">C-OPS-02</span> | S | The `sandloom outbox purge` CLI entry point itself is not invoked by a test. |
| <span class="sl-id">C-PROJ-03</span> | S | --tenant scoping of a rebuild is not exercised by a test. |
| <span class="sl-id">C-PROJ-04</span> | S | No test (framework or examples) uses insert_only; a unit test proving INSERT seeds and UPDATE preserves the column is missing. |
| <span class="sl-id">C-TENANT-02</span> | S | TenantScope(required=False) yielding None and leaving the context unbound, and custom header/claim_keys, are untested. |
| <span class="sl-id">G-AUDIT-01</span> | S | No generic test that a plain record_audit followed by a UoW rollback leaves no audit_log row; only the block_user path proves it. |
| <span class="sl-id">G-AUDIT-02</span> | S | The 'no audit store' branch of AuditUnavailableError (database driver without the audit feature) has no direct raising test (test_audit_store_skips_unsupported_backend only checks the store is absent). |
| <span class="sl-id">G-COMPAT-03</span> | S | No test drives `sandloom contracts check --against http://<provider>` (live describe document over the internal token) or the `sandloom contracts snapshot --write/--check` CLI exit codes (only the underlying functions are tested). |
| <span class="sl-id">G-COMPAT-07</span> | S | The startup log for a remote binding with no snapshot at all ("unchecked", CONTRACT_SNAPSHOT_PATHS absent) is not asserted. |
| <span class="sl-id">G-CONFIG-05</span> | S | sandloom_config_override_active{setting,kind} metric export (app_factory) is not asserted by any test. |
| <span class="sl-id">G-CONFIG-08</span> | S | AGENTS.md and accepted_risks error messages point at docs/reference/configuration-tiers.md, but that file does not exist in the repo (only tiers.render_markdown() in memory); nothing checks the committed page exists / is current. |
| <span class="sl-id">G-EFFECT-03</span> | S | No test proves that a before_commit check registered inside a rolled-back savepoint is skipped (ADR §3 stage 1). |
| <span class="sl-id">G-EVENT-05</span> | S | No test asserts the handler's DB writes are rolled back when the handler raises (the consumer UoW rollback itself); tests check redelivery with fake sessions only. |
| <span class="sl-id">G-GUARD-01</span> | S | Tests call the order checker directly; no test boots create_app with a misordered route to prove the startup wiring. |
| <span class="sl-id">G-INFRA-06</span> | S | no test asserts the preflight performs no I/O (opens no provider/connection), nor that a failed required preflight aborts create_app for a required module |
| <span class="sl-id">G-MIGRATE-05</span> | S | Doc drift: AGENTS.md lists four core tables (outbox/audit/consumer_inbox/contract_command_log) but the chain (and the test) also own http_idempotency_log. |
| <span class="sl-id">G-MIGRATE-06</span> | S | The prod refusal of ensure-outbox --apply without --force (cli/migrate.py) is untested. |
| <span class="sl-id">G-MODULE-03</span> | S | no test proves a module importing sandloom.core.module_api._service_registry or sandloom.core.facade._state is flagged (only that the tree is clean) |
| <span class="sl-id">G-OPS-12</span> | S | The prod --confirm-production requirement of sandloom security is untested (only sandloom backup's guard rails test it). |
| <span class="sl-id">G-OUTBOX-04</span> | S | No test calls publish_event INSIDE a UoW with an invalid channel / schema-violating / oversized payload and asserts the call raises and no outbox_messages row exists; the in-UoW path (unit_of_work/effects.py preflight) is only covered indirectly. |
| <span class="sl-id">G-PROFILE-05</span> | S | enforce_runtime is tested directly, but no test proves it is wired as a critical startup task of create_app's lifespan or of the Celery worker boot (removing either call site would stay green). |
| <span class="sl-id">G-PROFILE-06</span> | S | The 'Cannot attest separate ... Redis processes' failure (deployment_identity raising) has no test. |
| <span class="sl-id">G-REVOKE-06</span> | S | No test pins that password change/reset and user deactivation use the immediate (pre-commit) path specifically, rather than only that tokens end up revoked. |
| <span class="sl-id">G-RISK-02</span> | S | Export of sandloom_accepted_risk_active{risk}=1 (app_factory) is never asserted; a test reading the metric after create_app in prod with a risk accepted is missing. |
| <span class="sl-id">G-RISK-11</span> | S | No test exercises the unversioned_ddl_repair gate in sandloom/core/cli/migrate.py (only ensure-outbox dry-run / dev apply are tested). |
| <span class="sl-id">G-RLS-05</span> | S | The BYPASSRLS-attribute branch (and membership in a BYPASSRLS/superuser role) has no direct test; only SUPERUSER, table ownership and system-role membership are exercised. |
| <span class="sl-id">G-RLS-08</span> | S | 'No audit row, no commit' (a failing audit write aborts the system session's commit) and the structured start/end log record (op_id, outcome, duration) are not tested. |
| <span class="sl-id">G-TENANT-14</span> | S | The 'token tenant does not match the configured tenant' 403 (token claim, no header) branch has no test. |
| <span class="sl-id">G-TENANT-17</span> | S | The rule is only tested at the analyzer level (find_unsafe_tenant_sql); no test runs it through run_checks/sandloom check on a module fixture as the tenant-scoped-models rule is. |
| <span class="sl-id">G-UOW-06</span> | S | Only the private resolver is unit-tested; no end-to-end test holds DbSession + Database("x") in one endpoint and asserts the event lands in the chosen database's outbox_messages (and is marked delivered there). |
| <span class="sl-id">G-UOW-07</span> | S | Non-atomicity itself is a documented non-guarantee; no test pins that a failing second-database UoW leaves the first committed (i.e. that nobody quietly introduces a coupled commit). |
| <span class="sl-id">G-BLOCK-04</span> | M | No generic check forces a custom (app-defined) issuer to call ensure_user_not_blocked; the rule is documentation-only for third-party issuers. |
| <span class="sl-id">G-MODULE-17</span> | M | convention only: no sandloom check rule or test rejects a ForeignKey from one module's table to another module's table prefix |

## Removed

| Id | Statement | Reason | Approved | Date |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| C-TEST-04 | sandloom.core.testing.assert_operation_classes(app) fails an app with an unclassified or contradictorily classified route; sandloom new generates the check. | superseded by C-TEST-07 (ADR-0009, accepted by the owner; spec §9.2): ADR-0009 removes assert_operation_classes outright; apps assert deny-by-default with sandloom.sdk.testing.route_policy(route) and pin their routes with assert_route_snapshot (C-TEST-07). | owner (ADR-0009 / ADR-0010 approval, 2026-10-25) | 2026-10-26 |
| G-GUARD-03 | create_app refuses (FinancialGuardError) an operation_class('F') route with a response-storing cache guard or a fail-open guard. | superseded by G-SENS-05 (ADR-0009, accepted by the owner; spec §9.2) | owner (ADR-0009 / ADR-0010 approval, 2026-10-25) | 2026-10-26 |
| G-IDEM-13 | create_app refuses an operation_class("F") route whose idempotency guard is the response-storing cache form or fail-open (FinancialGuardError); durable=True or store_response=False + fail_closed=True are accepted. | superseded by G-SENS-05 (ADR-0009, accepted by the owner; spec §9.2) | owner (ADR-0009 / ADR-0010 approval, 2026-10-25) | 2026-10-26 |
| G-OPCLASS-01 | Every API route of the composed monolith (kernel ops routes + identity + tenancy + billing) declares exactly one ADR-0003 operation class (P/R/RS/W/F/A) on the route or its router; an unclassified route fails CI, and apps run the same gate via sandloom.core.testing.assert_operation_classes(app). | superseded by G-ROUTE-01 (ADR-0009, accepted by the owner; spec §9.2) | owner (ADR-0009 / ADR-0010 approval, 2026-10-25) | 2026-10-26 |
| G-OPCLASS-02 | create_app refuses (OperationClassError) a route with two different classes, an unknown class, a revocation_freshness budget outside class R, or a class RS/W/F/A route that is not always-strict. | superseded by G-ROUTE-01 / G-ROUTE-04 (ADR-0009, accepted by the owner; spec §9.2) | owner (ADR-0009 / ADR-0010 approval, 2026-10-25) | 2026-10-26 |
| G-REVOKE-13 | revocation_freshness(max_staleness_s=N) requires 0 < N <= 5 (else ValueError) and may be declared only on GET/HEAD routes: create_app refuses a budget on any other method or on a router with a write route (RevocationPolicyError). | superseded by G-REVOKE-21 (ADR-0009, accepted by the owner; spec §9.2) | owner (ADR-0009 / ADR-0010 approval, 2026-10-25) | 2026-10-26 |
| G-REVOKE-14 | A budgeted route answers from a per-process mark copy only while it is younger than the budget at DECISION time (re-checked after the live block read); a copy is never extended, and a copy expired or invalidated while a read was in flight is replaced by a live read of the mark. | superseded by G-REVOKE-21 (ADR-0009, accepted by the owner; spec §9.2) | owner (ADR-0009 / ADR-0010 approval, 2026-10-25) | 2026-10-26 |
| G-REVOKE-15 | revoke_user_tokens drops the local copy and broadcasts on Redis pub/sub (sandloom:auth:revocations); other processes drop theirs, a lost broadcast delays a revocation on budgeted routes by at most the budget, only a drop of the same subject (or a wholesale clear on (re)subscribe) discards an in-flight read. | superseded by G-REVOKE-21 (ADR-0009, accepted by the owner; spec §9.2) | owner (ADR-0009 / ADR-0010 approval, 2026-10-25) | 2026-10-26 |
| G-REVOKE-16 | A route marked always-strict (Depends(strict_revocation()) on it or its router, or a path under AUTH_REVOCATION_STRICT_PATH_PREFIXES) ignores a revocation_freshness budget (logged at startup) and always reads the mark live. | superseded by G-REVOKE-21 (ADR-0009, accepted by the owner; spec §9.2) | owner (ADR-0009 / ADR-0010 approval, 2026-10-25) | 2026-10-26 |
| G-REVOKE-20 | Per-request revocation cost: a strict route does one Redis round trip (MGET of revocation + block marks); a budgeted route with a fresh local copy does one GET of the block mark. | superseded by G-REVOKE-21 (ADR-0009, accepted by the owner; spec §9.2) | owner (ADR-0009 / ADR-0010 approval, 2026-10-25) | 2026-10-26 |
